item.title: Gas supply cut to power plants to manage LNG shortage
item.description:
Petrobangla has reduced gas supply to power plants to manage a shortage in the national grid following the shutdown of Summit’s floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal for maintenance, aiming to maintain supplies to industrial, household and compressed natural gas (CNG) consumers.
According to Petrobangla's supply data, gas-fired power plants generated 4,600MW of electricity on Tuesday. Generation dropped to 3,500MW on Wednesday, marking a decline of around 1,100MW in a single day.
However, the Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) said the reduction did not result in an electricity shortage. Its data showed that electricity demand stood at 13,135MW at 4pm on Wednesday, with the entire demand being met.
An official of Titas Gas said gas supply had declined, but demand was also relatively low as garment factories were closed.
The official said the reduction in gas supply for power generation had not caused an electricity shortage, as power was still being generated using other fuels.
Meanwhile, residential consumers continue to face difficulties due to low gas pressure. Consumers in several areas are experiencing problems cooking as gas pressure in household stoves remains low. Gas pressure at CNG stations has also been affected.
Petrobangla's data showed that the country's total gas supply stood at 2,540 million cubic feet at 8am on Wednesday. It fell to 2,079 million cubic feet at 10am before rising slightly to 2,110 million cubic feet at 2pm.
The 2pm supply level was 430 million cubic feet lower than the supply recorded at 8am.
At 8am on Wednesday, domestic gas fields supplied 1,566 million cubic feet, while imported LNG accounted for 974 million cubic feet.
At 10am, regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) supply fell to 514 million cubic feet. It increased slightly to 540 million cubic feet by 2pm, while supply from domestic gas fields remained almost unchanged during the period.
Summit's floating LNG terminal has been shut down for 80 hours for routine maintenance. The terminal will remain out of operation from Tuesday to Thursday, reducing LNG supply to the national grid during this period.
Petrobangla had earlier warned that the shutdown would result in low gas pressure.
Relevant sources said a combined-cycle power plant requires around 20 million cubic feet of gas per day to generate every 100MW of electricity.
Accordingly, reducing power generation by 1,100MW lowers daily gas demand by around 220 million cubic feet. The reduction in gas consumption by power plants is intended to help manage the supply shortage in other sectors.

item.title: 57 of DSCC’s 75 wards at dengue risk, 29 classified as high-risk
item.description:
At least 57 of the 75 wards under Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) have recorded Aedes mosquito density above the prescribed threshold, with 29 classified as high-risk areas, according to a recent survey conducted by the city corporation.
The findings were revealed on Wednesday at the publication of the results of the 2026 monsoon Aedes mosquito larvae survey at the Nagar Bhaban auditorium.
The 12-day survey was conducted between September 27 and October 8.
A total of 2,250 houses were randomly selected as samples, with 30 houses surveyed in each of DSCC’s 75 wards.
Thirty-six field workers from DSCC and the Communicable Disease Control (CDC) unit of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) took part in the survey. The digital data collection platform KoboToolbox was used to ensure accuracy in gathering information.
According to the survey, Aedes mosquito larvae and pupae were found in 322 of the 2,250 houses inspected, meaning approximately 14.31% of the sampled houses showed evidence of Aedes mosquito breeding.
Photo: Courtesy
Among different types of buildings, single-unit houses recorded the highest proportion of larvae and pupae at 31.37%, closely followed by multistorey buildings at 31.06%.
The corresponding rates were 17.39% in semi-pucca houses, 13.04% in buildings under construction and 7.14% in vacant plots.
Plastic buckets were identified as the most common breeding sites, accounting for 14.21% of the larvae found during the survey. Other major breeding sites included plastic drums at 11.22%, stagnant water in basements at 9.98%, plastic mugs at 9.23% and flower pots at 5.99%.
The ward-wise risk assessment classified 29 wards as high-risk, 28 as medium-risk and 18 as general-risk areas. This means all 75 wards under the corporation fall into one of the three risk categories.
The survey assessed mosquito density and breeding conditions using four indicators: the Breteau Index (BI), House Index (HI), Container Index (CI) and Pupal Index (PI). These indices were used to evaluate potential dengue hotspots.
The 29 high-risk wards are distributed across eight administrative zones.
In Zone 1, wards 15, 16, 19, 20 and 21 were identified as high-risk. In Zone 2, the list includes wards 1, 2, 9, 11, 12 and 13.
In Zone 3, wards 14, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 55 and 56 were classified as high-risk, while ward 31 in Zone 4 and wards 43 and 44 in Zone 5 also made the list.
Ward 71 in Zone 7, wards 62 and 65 in Zone 9, and wards 58, 59, 60 and 61 in Zone 10 were also identified as high-risk areas.
Speaking at the event, DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam said the corporation was working to ensure zero dengue-related deaths in Dhaka South this year.
“We do not want even a single person to die of dengue,” he said, adding that the special Aedes mosquito larvae survey was conducted for the first time in Dhaka to achieve this goal.
He said the survey had provided important information that would help make mosquito control activities more effective. He expressed hope that these efforts would further reduce the number of dengue cases.
Emphasising the importance of public awareness, the administrator said that although the city corporation had taken various initiatives, residents needed to become more proactive in preventing dengue.
He claimed that removing stagnant water from individual homes could reduce dengue prevalence by up to 80%.
He urged residents to ensure that water did not accumulate on rooftops, in flower pots, beneath refrigerators or in nearby drains.
Regarding cleanliness in government buildings, Salam said regular cleaning of premises, including areas behind government offices, had been undertaken following the prime minister's directive. He noted that these areas had remained neglected for a long time.
He also announced that special cleanliness drives and awareness programmes would be conducted every Saturday at all primary schools under Dhaka South as part of the dengue prevention campaign.

item.title: Garment unrest eases after eight days as workers return to factories
item.description:
The garment sector showed signs of returning to normal on Thursday after eight days of unrest over minimum wages, with workers resuming production across major industrial belts in Savar, Gazipur and Narayanganj, although sporadic protests in Ashulia forced 70 factories to suspend operations.
The improvement came after days of demonstrations, clashes with police and widespread factory closures that disrupted production in the country’s largest export-earning industry.
While most factories resumed operations, uncertainty over the proposed minimum wage continued to fuel isolated demonstrations, particularly in Ashulia, where workers blocked roads and clashed with police.
Authorities reinforced security across industrial areas, deploying 33 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to prevent further disruptions and facilitate the resumption of factory operations.
The government has already formed a wage board to review workers’ pay, with a revised wage structure expected to take effect in December.
However, the amount of the proposed increase has yet to be announced.
Workers have been demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, arguing that rising living costs have made their existing salaries inadequate.
Factories in Savar and the Dhaka Export Processing Zone (DEPZ) resumed production Thursday morning after several days of disruption.
Workers entered their workplaces peacefully, while additional police and BGB personnel remained stationed outside important industrial establishments in Ashulia and Hemayetpur.
Normal operations also resumed across much of Gazipur, including Shafipur, Chandra and Palli Bidyut in Kaliakair, as well as Bhogra Bypass, Konabari, Kashimpur and Salna.
Workers joined their respective shifts without major disruption, bringing relief to factory management after several days of uncertainty.
The situation in Narayanganj also remained largely calm, with workers returning to their workplaces.
Despite the broader improvement, Ashulia witnessed fresh demonstrations as workers continued demanding clarity over the proposed wage increase.
Workers at several factories initially joined their shifts around 8am and registered attendance before leaving their workplaces and gathering outside nearby factories.
Some demonstrators urged workers from neighbouring establishments to join the protests, prompting factory authorities to suspend operations.
Industrial Police-1 Superintendent Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said 70 of the 1,863 factories under his jurisdiction had declared holidays, while the remaining factories continued operating.
He described the overall situation as stable despite isolated disturbances.
Protesters blocked the Abdullahpur-Baipail road, disrupting traffic before police intervened to clear the highway.
Clashes subsequently erupted in Jamgora, where some protesters allegedly threw bricks and stones at police and vandalised police vehicles.
Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse the demonstrators.
Mominul said the unrest began after some workers were dismissed and police detained several individuals during the demonstrations.
He also alleged that outsiders were attempting to provoke workers and disrupt factory operations, including through social media.
Authorities deployed 33 BGB platoons across major industrial areas as part of efforts to maintain order and prevent further disruption.
According to BGB headquarters, three platoons were deployed in Mirpur, 11 in Savar and Ashulia, 12 in Gazipur and seven in Narayanganj.
Armoured personnel carriers, riot control vehicles and drones were being used to strengthen security and monitor developments.
BGB personnel were also equipped with body-worn cameras, while a monitoring cell at headquarters was overseeing the situation around the clock.
Meanwhile, the Detective Branch arrested eight more people in connection with Tuesday’s attack on police during garment workers’ demonstrations in Mirpur-11.
DMP Deputy Commissioner Md Akhtar Hossain said investigators identified the suspects through CCTV footage and technological assistance.
Although production has resumed in most industrial areas, the dispute over wages remains unresolved.
The government has formed a minimum wage board and announced plans to introduce a revised wage structure from December, but workers have yet to receive confirmation of the proposed minimum amount.
Industrial Police officials said factory owners were committed to implementing the revised structure once finalised.
The latest developments follow protests that began in Mirpur on October 29 and subsequently spread to Ashulia, Gazipur, Savar and Narayanganj.
The demonstrations triggered repeated clashes, road blockades and temporary factory closures, with at least 529 factories suspending production at one stage.
“In Sha Allah, the board (newly formed wage board) will set a new minimum wage within the next one to two months so that our dear workers can live a little better.”

item.title: World Bank: Bangladesh’s external debt rises to $113.4bn
item.description:
Bangladesh’s total external debt climbed 8.6 percent to reach $113.4 billion in 2025, according to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, even as the country maintained manageable debt-to-GNI and debt-service ratios amid a broader global financing squeeze.
The new report reveals that Bangladesh’s long-term public and publicly guaranteed (PPG) external debt stands at $89.5 billion. Multilateral creditors hold the majority share of these public obligations at $51.1 billion—primarily driven by the World Bank’s International Development Association ($22.6 billion) and the Asian Development Bank ($17.5 billion).
Bilateral debt accounts for $32.6 billion, anchored by major partners like Japan ($12.7 billion) and the Russian Federation ($9.0 billion).
Private nonguaranteed debt of $9.9 billion and $14.1 billion in short-term liabilities make up the remainder of the nation's external profile.
Despite the rising debt stock, Bangladesh’s macro-fiscal indicators reflect resilience compared to regional peers.
The country's external debt-to-GNI ratio stood at a moderate 24 percent, while the debt service-to-exports ratio eased by 3.1% to 16%.
Official commitments extended to Bangladesh also retained favorable terms, featuring an average maturity of 25 years, a 6-year grace period, and an average interest rate of 3%.
Zooming out to the regional picture, total external debt across South Asia reached $955 billion in 2025.
While regional debt-to-GNI ratios remain contained at an average of 21 percent, South Asian economies face an increasingly unforgiving global capital environment.
On a global scale, total external debt across all low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) surged 5.5% to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, marking the sharpest increase in four years as private lenders and bond markets forcefully reopened.
However, this renewed market access has come at an exorbitant price, particularly for the poorest economies. Private creditors charged IDA-eligible countries an average interest rate of 8.2% on new commitments in 2025—the highest level seen since the late 1980s.
Total debt service payments for LMICs rose for the fifth consecutive year to $1.4 trillion, consuming over 40% of government revenues in vulnerable nations and crowding out vital spending on health, education, and infrastructure.
Commenting on the global outlook, World Bank Chief Statistician Haishan Fu warned that access to finance is not enough.
“We must know the debt, understand its terms, and ensure that the financing developing economies receive strengthens rather than constrains their ability to grow, withstand shocks, and improve the lives of their people."
Adding to this, World Bank analysts noted a troubling paradox where developing nations are borrowing more and paying steeper prices, ultimately leaving fewer resources available for long-term sustainable development.

item.title: July atrocities: ICT accepts charges against Amu, 6 others
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Thursday took cognisance of charges against seven individuals linked to the Awami League, including former minister Amir Hossain Amu, in a case filed over crimes against humanity committed during the July 2024 uprising.
The three-member bench of the ICT-2, led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, also ordered that six of the accused, who were in jail, be produced before it on November 22 in connection with the case.
It issued a warrant for the arrest of Awami League Organising Secretary Mirza Azam, who had been absconding.
The other accused in the cases were former Shipping Minister Shajahan Khan, former Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Lt Col (retd) Faruk Khan, former Agricultural Minister Abdur Razzaque, former minister Dr Dipu Moni and former Energy Adviser to the ousted Prime Minister Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury.
Briefing reporters, Prosecutor Gazi Tamim said former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina had taken state-level and political decisions to suppress the July mass uprising.
Plans had been devised to use lethal weapons against protesters, impose a curfew, shut down the internet and control the media, he said.
Records of conversations, documents, supporting evidence and witness statements had been submitted to the tribunal in support of these allegations, Tamim added.
He said various pieces of evidence, including a United Nations report, had been submitted to support allegations that state forces and intelligence agencies had been used to carry out killings to suppress the movement.
The prosecutor also claimed that the UN report had contained an alleged instruction by Sheikh Hasina to "kill them and hide the bodies."
Regarding the individual roles of the accused, he said the prosecution had presented information that Tk 5 crore in cash had been found in sacks at the residence of Amu after August 5, 2024.
Faruk Khan attended a security committee meeting on August 4, where a decision had allegedly been taken to shoot and kill protesters at the entry points to Dhaka on August 5, according to the prosecution.
Dipu Moni, meanwhile, had participated in a meeting on imposing the curfew and had been involved in planning to suppress the movement, Tamim alleged.
He also claimed that Shajahan Khan, through conversations with Sheikh Hasina, had issued instructions to deploy police, Awami League leaders and activists, and workers against the protesters.
The case also includes allegations of arson at various establishments during the movement.
The prosecutor said recordings of conversations involving Sheikh Hasina, Obaidul Quader and Hasan Mahmud had been submitted to the tribunal in this regard.
Forensic reports verifying the authenticity of the recordings, along with video reports verified by experts from the BBC, Al Jazeera and the United Nations, had also been submitted, he added.
Tamim said the seven accused had been charged with incitement, assistance, conspiracy and contribution to the commission of crimes. They also face allegations of superior command responsibility.
The prosecution alleged that the accused, from their respective positions, played roles in making and implementing political decisions to suppress the movement.
The prosecutor further said the investigation into the abduction and torture of six coordinators of the July uprising while in the custody of the Detective Branch (DB) was nearing completion.
Earlier, on November 2, the prosecution submitted formal charges against the seven leaders.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: Bangladesh wants Hasina extradited from India
item.description:
Referring to the existing extradition treaty with India, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said they want former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who now faces the death penalty, to be handed over to Bangladesh.
“We want Hasina to be handed over. She will be handed over. She is a terrorist. She is a fled criminal. There is an active extradition treaty between Bangladesh and India,” he told reporters, noting that there is no need to issue her a passport.
Kobir made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport after seeing off Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee.
Hasina, ousted in a mass uprising in 2024, has told The Associated Press that she remains committed to returning to Bangladesh from exile in India next month, despite being sentenced to death over her government's deadly crackdown on protesters.
“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told AP in response to questions by email. “So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed.”
Hasina fled to India after student-led protests forced her from power and has remained there ever since.
In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.
Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina’s extradition, but India has declined to hand her over. She first announced in August her intention to return in December.
On October 3, Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi stressed that former Prime Minister Hasina was not brought to India by the Indian Air Force or the Indian Army. He said the legal process concerning Bangladesh’s request for her extradition was ongoing and that no timeframe could be given as the courts were involved.
“To give you a straight answer, again and again, the government of India, through the Spokesperson at the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), has replied to this that there is a process, and the process involves legality, and it is well structured. So, as far as that is concerned, the process is on,” Trivedi said.
He said the courts were involved in the matter and, therefore, “nobody can give you a timeframe.”
Trivedi said Hasina was still the Prime Minister of Bangladesh when she arrived in India, and New Delhi had to respond to the situation as a neighboring country.
“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that. It was our duty as a neighbor to accept the reality of life, because situations are such where at times you are not prepared for it,” the Indian envoy said.
Trivedi also referred to the circumstances under which Hasina came to India after leaving Bangladesh in August 2024, saying the Indian authorities were not prepared for the situation.
“Going back to history, Hasina Ji was not brought to India by the Indian Air Force or Indian Army,” he said, referring to the circumstances surrounding her departure from Bangladesh.
He said the situation unfolded because of “tragic circumstances” in Bangladesh at the time, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world, where innocent people get killed, regardless of which part of the world it is.
He questioned what India's alternative could have been under those circumstances. “What was our choice? If you would have said that no, we are not going to accept, we don’t give landing permission. Things would have been I don’t know what,” Trivedi said.
Bangladesh has repeatedly requested India to extradite Hasina, who has been staying in India since her departure from Bangladesh in August 2024.
The issue was also raised by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during his meeting with Trivedi in Dhaka in August.
India’s Ministry of External Affairs subsequently said that Bangladesh’s request was being examined in line with established procedures.

item.title: BB updates Tk20,000cr support scheme for defunct industries
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has restructured and renamed its Tk20,000 crore financial support initiative to inject greater dynamism into its operations.
The central bank’s Banking Regulation and Policy Department (BRPD) issued a circular letter (BRPD-1 Circular Letter No. 37) on Thursday, introducing these key amendments.
Under the updated directives, the scheme—originally titled the "Closed Industry and Service Sector Facilitation Pre-Finance Scheme"—has been officially renamed the "Closed Industry and Service Sector Facilitation Re-Finance Scheme."
Consequently, all references to "Pre-finance scheme" in previous circulars and circular letters dated June 4, July 7, and September 17, 2026, have been replaced with "Re-finance scheme".
The program is now formally designated as a refinancing scheme rather than pre-financing.
Banks must now collect a formal declaration from loan seekers confirming that they have no prior history of money laundering, forgery, fund diversion, or misuse of loan funds.
Borrowers will receive priority when applying for loans under this scheme from the same bank that extended their original project loan.
All transactions utilizing funds provided under this scheme must be conducted through the customer's Escrow Account or Revenue Account, strictly adhering to prior central bank instructions regarding project income account openings (BRPD Circular No. 01, dated January 18, 2024).
Participating banks must sanction loans with the approval of their board of directors or the board’s executive committee.
Applications for refinancing, along with necessary data and documentation in a prescribed format (Annexure-A), must be submitted to the Director of BRPD-3 at Bangladesh Bank’s head office within the week following loan disbursement.
If a bank fails to apply within the subsequent week, an application may still be submitted within an additional 15 days by providing valid reasons.
The central bank issued these orders under the authority conferred by Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, and the instructions take effect immediately.
Corresponding participation agreements executed with banks will be deemed amended in alignment with these changes.

item.title: 33 platoons of BGB deployed in Dhaka, industrial areas
item.description:
A total of 33 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in different industrial areas of Dhaka and its surrounding districts to ensure the security of garment factories and maintain law and order.
Of the deployed personnel, three platoons are stationed in Mirpur, 11 in Savar and Ashulia, 12 in Gazipur and seven in Narayanganj.
The activities are being monitored and coordinated round the clock by a monitoring cell at the BGB headquarters, says BGB headquarters public relation officer Shariful Islam on Thursday morning.
Armoured Personnel Carriers (APCs) and Riot Control Vehicles (RCVs) have also been deployed to strengthen security and tackle any untoward situation.
To make security operations more effective, live monitoring is being conducted through drones.
Body-worn cameras and improvised body-worn cameras are also being used by BGB personnel while performing their duties.
BGB members remain on alert in coordination with the local administration and police to maintain a peaceful environment in the industrial areas and deal with any possible untoward situation.
The overall situation in the areas concerned is being closely monitored, he said.
The BGB's security operations will continue to ensure public safety, maintain a normal working environment in the industrial areas and keep the law and order situation under control.

item.title: PM lays foundation stone for Tk4,068cr Mongla Port project
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday laid the foundation stone for a Tk4,068 crore project to construct two container jetties and develop supporting infrastructure to expand and modernise Mongla Port.

item.title: Word Bank: Bangladesh’s foreign debt surges 8.6% to $113.4bn
item.description:
Bangladesh’s total external debt climbed 8.6% to $113.4 billion in 2025, according to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, underscoring the country’s growing reliance on foreign financing at a time when developing economies face mounting debt-servicing pressures.
Despite the increase, Bangladesh maintained a relatively moderate external debt burden, with outstanding foreign liabilities equivalent to 24% of gross national income (GNI), while its debt service-to-exports ratio eased to 16%.
The report shows that long-term public and publicly guaranteed (PPG) external debt reached $89.5 billion, accounting for nearly four-fifths of the country’s total external obligations.
Multilateral creditors remained the largest source of public external financing, holding $51.1 billion in outstanding debt.
The World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) accounted for $22.6 billion, followed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) with $17.5 billion.
Bilateral creditors held another $32.6 billion, with Japan accounting for $12.7 billion and Russia $9 billion.
The remaining external liabilities included $9.9 billion in private nonguaranteed debt and $14.1 billion in short-term borrowing.
Although Bangladesh’s external debt stock continued to expand, several indicators suggested that the immediate burden remained within manageable levels.
The country’s external debt-to-GNI ratio stood at 24%, while the debt service-to-exports ratio declined to 16%, reflecting an improvement in the proportion of export earnings required to meet external debt obligations.
The terms of new official financing commitments also remained relatively favourable.
According to the World Bank, these commitments carried an average maturity of 25 years, a six-year grace period and an average interest rate of 3%.
Such financing conditions provide borrowers with longer repayment periods and lower borrowing costs than those generally available through international commercial markets.
However, the growing debt stock underscores the importance of maintaining export earnings, foreign exchange reserves and sustainable repayment capacity.
Bangladesh’s rising external debt comes amid a broader increase in borrowing across South Asia.
The region’s total external debt reached $955 billion in 2025, although its average debt-to-GNI ratio remained relatively contained at 21%.
Bangladesh’s ratio of 24% was slightly above the regional average, indicating a somewhat higher external debt burden relative to national income.
Despite relatively moderate debt ratios, South Asian economies face an increasingly challenging global financing environment, with higher borrowing costs and pressure on public finances.
Globally, total external debt across low- and middle-income countries rose 5.5% to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, marking the sharpest annual increase in four years.
The rise followed renewed activity in international bond markets and increased lending by private creditors.
However, the improved access to financing came at a substantially higher cost for poorer economies.
Private creditors charged countries eligible for IDA financing an average interest rate of 8.2% on new commitments in 2025, the highest level since the late 1980s.
Meanwhile, total debt-service payments by low- and middle-income countries increased for the fifth consecutive year, reaching $1.4 trillion.
In some vulnerable economies, debt repayments consumed more than 40% of government revenue, limiting resources available for healthcare, education and infrastructure development.
World Bank Chief Statistician Haishan Fu warned that access to financing alone would not ensure sustainable development.
“We must know the debt, understand its terms, and ensure that the financing developing economies receive strengthens rather than constrains their ability to grow, withstand shocks, and improve the lives of their people,” she said.
World Bank analysts cautioned that developing economies were increasingly borrowing at higher costs, potentially reducing the resources available for long-term economic development.

Islami Bank to increase authorised capital by Tk 80 billion
item.description:
Islami Bank has decided to increase its authorised capital from Tk 20 billion to Tk 100 billion. The decision was taken at a meeting of the bank’s board of directors held on 4 November.

As a listed company, the bank informed its shareholders of the decision through the stock exchanges yesterday, Thursday.

Speaking on condition of anonymity about the decision to increase the bank's capital, a senior bank official told Prothom Alo, “The bank has fallen into a capital crisis due to irregularities by the S Alam Group. We are therefore trying to bring a foreign strategic investor on board by increasing the authorised capital. The recommendation to raise the capital came from Bangladesh Bank. We hope Bangladesh Bank will approve our decision.”

S Alam out, Al-Arafah Islami Bank now under KDS' control

According to the announcement made by Islami Bank to the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), the decision to increase authorised capital will be implemented through necessary amendments to the bank’s memorandum of association.

It will take effect subject to approval from Bangladesh Bank and other regulatory authorities, as well as final approval by shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting.

It is learnt that Islami Bank Bangladesh posted a net loss of Tk 33.03 billion after tax in the first nine months (January-September) of the current calendar year.

S Alam group laundered Tk 2.25 trillion: BFIU report

In contrast, the bank had earned a profit of around Tk 790 million in the first nine months of the previous year. The bank also incurred a loss of Tk 19.76 billion in the first quarter (July-September) of the 2026-27 fiscal year.

According to the bank’s data, its asset value has fallen by nearly half due to the huge losses. As of 30 September, the bank’s net asset value (NAV) stood at Tk 35.84 billion, compared with Tk 69.63 billion during the same period last year. As a result, its net asset value per share has also declined.

Islami Bank, which is facing a financial crisis, has been unable to pay any dividends to its shareholders since 2023. As a result, the bank is now classified in the Z category as a low-grade company on the stock market.

A mysterious visit by S Alam to Islami Bank

The S Alam Group of Chattogram took control of Islami Bank in 2017. Since then, the group has withdrawn nearly Tk 1 trillion from the bank through loans taken in its own name and under other names. All of those loans have now become defaulted.

The S Alam Group lost control of the bank after the Awami League government was ousted in the mass uprising on 5 August 2024. During the interim government’s tenure, independent directors were given responsibility for running the bank. Bangladesh Bank has now taken over its management.

item.title: Bangladesh Parliamentary Caucus on Migration, Rights and Development launched to strengthen migrant rights and accountability
item.description:
The Bangladesh Parliamentary Caucus on Migration, Rights and Development was formally inaugurated on Wednesday, 4 November 2026 at The Westin Dhaka, bringing together parliamentarians, government representatives, development partners and international organizations, CSOs, media, trade union, private sector and migration experts to strengthen migration governance and protect the rights of Bangladeshi migrant workers, reports a press release.

The programme was attended by the speaker of parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, as chief guest, deputy speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal, as special guest, and state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam with state minister for expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment Md Nurul Haque as guests of honour. The event was chaired by caucus chairperson ABM Mosharraf Hossain.

Diversification of migration destination: Focusing on talent partnership programme

Mahmuda Habiba, secretary general of the caucus delivered her opening speech and introduced the parliamentary caucus executive and general members. Syed Saiful Haque, chairman, WARBE DF, secretariat of the parliamentary caucus delivered his welcome speech.

In his address, Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad said, “Migration is not just about remittances sent from abroad; it is also about the rights, dignity and security of our people.” Highlighting the hardships faced by migrant workers, particularly women, he stressed the need for stronger enforcement of migration laws and better protection in destination countries. He also called for Bangladesh to be developed as a migration destination and urged parliamentarians to use the caucus as a platform to facilitate overseas employment and monitor the implementation of migration laws at the grassroots.

Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal highlighted the contribution of migrant workers to the national economy, stating, “The remittances sent by migrant workers are a driving force of our economy.” He also stressed the need for diplomatic missions to take stronger measures to protect migrant workers' rights and address exploitation abroad.

State minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam and state minister for expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment Md Nurul Haque highlighted the importance of government initiatives and institutional coordination in addressing migration-related challenges, and ensuring better services and protection for migrant workers.

The panel discussion brought attention to persistent challenges in the migration sector, including high recruitment costs, unregulated intermediaries, human trafficking and gaps in the implementation of existing policies. Panelists also emphasised the importance of fair recruitment, psychosocial and socioeconomic protection, and stronger coordination between the ministries of foreign affairs and home affairs to address human trafficking.

Female worker migration rises, but remains dependent on two countries

At the event solidarity statements were delivered by Kazi Faisal Bin Seraj, country representative, The Asia Foundation; James Goldman, deputy high commissioner and development director to Bangladesh, British High Commission, Dhaka; Max Tuñón, country director, International Labour Organization (ILO) in Bangladesh; Laura Tomm Bonde, chief of mission, International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Bangladesh; Diepak Elmer, deputy head of mission / head of cooperation, Embassy of Switzerland in Bangladesh; Antonio Alessandro, ambassador, Embassy of Italy in Dhaka; and Ambassador Nahida Sobhan, rector, Foreign Service Academy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The newly inaugurated all-party Caucus will serve as a dedicated parliamentary platform to advance evidence-based policy reform, strengthen oversight and ensure that the concerns of migrant workers are reflected in national decision-making. It will also promote stronger coordination among parliamentarians, government institutions, civil society and development partners.

The inauguration calls for collective commitment and coordinated action to ensure safe, orderly and regular migration, fair recruitment practices and the protection of the rights and dignity of Bangladeshi migrant workers. The programme was organised by the Caucus Secretariat, WARBE Development Foundation, with support from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and The Asia Foundation.

item.title: India makes visa mandatory for 6 minority groups from Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan
item.description:
India has made it mandatory for members of six non-Muslim communities from Bangladesh, Afghanistan and Pakistan who entered the country without valid travel documents, citing religious persecution, to obtain visas to continue staying there.
The Indian Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) amended the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025, through a notification issued on Wednesday, reports The Hindu.
The amendment requires Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from the three countries who entered India on or before December 31, 2024, to obtain an appropriate visa for their continued stay.
The provision applies to those who entered India without valid travel documents or whose documents have since expired, after being compelled to seek shelter due to religious persecution or fear of persecution.
The amendment retains an exemption introduced through a September 2, 2025 notification, which allowed members of the six communities to enter and stay in India without valid passports or visas.
However, the latest notification states that they must obtain an appropriate category of visa after entering India to continue their stay.
The 2025 exemption was issued under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, consolidating earlier notifications that exempted members of the communities from prosecution under passport and foreigners laws.
The amendment also aligns the exempted categories with India's Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, which provides a pathway to citizenship for members of the six non-Muslim communities from the three neighbouring countries who entered India before December 31, 2014.
The amendment also revises provisions governing travel between India, Nepal and Bhutan, introduces a formal definition of the Visa Manual and reorganises several categories of exemptions for foreign nationals.
The Visa Manual is defined as a central government-issued document containing instructions on visas, immigration and related matters.
Indian citizens travelling to Nepal or Bhutan, as well as Nepali and Bhutanese citizens entering or leaving India, will now have to produce identity documents specified in the manual before immigration authorities.
The passport exemption will not apply to Indian citizens using the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan borders to travel to third countries. Such travellers must carry valid passports and use designated immigration checkpoints.
Similarly, Nepali and Bhutanese citizens travelling to destinations other than India, Nepal or Bhutan, or those who have embarked from or transited through China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, must possess valid passports and visas.

item.title: Gold price drops by Tk2,739 per bhori
item.description:
Gold prices in Bangladesh fell by Tk2,739 per bhori on Friday, a day after a major increase, according to the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus).
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Friday.
Under the revised rates, 22-carat gold is priced at Tk2,26,937 per bhori (11.664 grams), down from Tk2,29,676 on Thursday.
The price of 22-carat gold has been set at Tk19,455 per gram.
The new rates were announced following a meeting of the Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Friday morning.
The association said the prices were adjusted in response to a decline in the price of pure gold in the local market.
According to the revised rates, 21-carat gold is priced at Tk18,580 per gram, 18-carat gold at Tk15,955, and traditional-method gold at Tk13,035.
Bajus has also reduced silver prices.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver is priced at Tk300 per gram, 21-carat silver at Tk290, 18-carat silver at Tk250, and traditional-method silver at Tk190.
Bajus said making charges will vary depending on the design of the jewellery.
VAT is included in the prescribed selling prices, so jewellers cannot charge it separately from customers.
For exchanges of old gold jewellery, a 12% deduction will apply to the prescribed price after excluding making charges and stone prices.
For purchases of old gold, an 18% deduction will apply.
VAT cannot be deducted separately in either case.
The revised prices will remain in effect at all jewellery shops across the country until further notice, Bajus said.
Gold prices in the domestic market have been adjusted 133 times this year, with 64 increases, 68 reductions and one VAT adjustment.
In 2025, Bajus adjusted gold prices 93 times, raising them 64 times and lowering them 29 times.
The number of price adjustments has increased significantly compared with last year, as fluctuations in pure gold prices in international and local markets have prompted frequent changes in domestic rates.

item.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
item.description:
Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms.

The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students.

Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on.

Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date.

The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features.

Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine.

If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.”

“No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote.

More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices.

In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages.

Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials.

The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini.

New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices.

“We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP.

The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy.

New York City Public Schools (NYCPS) are seeking more details from Google about the policy change, but the Gemini chatbot and AI mode are already disabled on Chromebooks used by students in NYC, a spokesperson for the district told AFP.

“NYCPS has also made requests to Google to disable the AI Overview displayed in the Google search result for students,” the spokesperson said.

In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.”

“We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said.

item.title: 90 million displaced people at climate risk in Bangladesh, other countries: UNHCR
item.description:
REFUGEES-CLIMATE/UN

Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people are living in countries increasingly exposed to climate-related droughts, floods and extreme heat, the UN refugee agency said on Friday, warning ahead of the COP31 climate summit that more funding is needed to help vulnerable communities adapt.

Nearly three-quarters of the world's forcibly displaced people are living in countries such as Afghanistan and Bangladesh that are exposed to severe climate-related risks, according to the report by the agency, known as UNHCR, published ahead of the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey. The findings show the overlap between conflict, displacement and climate change, the report said.

"Climate adaptation in fragile and displacement-affected areas is a matter of survival," said Anton Leis Garcia, UNHCR's assistant high commissioner for operations.

"We need climate financing to reach the communities where the needs are greatest," he said.

The report highlighted the experience of a Sudanese refugee who fled conflict in al-Fashir in June 2023 to the Farchana refugee settlement in eastern Chad. The refugee said she sometimes goes a week without finding safe water and must walk increasingly long distances for alternative sources as nearby seasonal riverbeds dry up amid intensifying heat.

Returns at risk

It also warned that climate change is making it harder for displaced people to return home sustainably.

In the first half of 2026, more than two-thirds of refugee returns were to countries highly exposed to climate hazards, placing them at risk of renewed displacement, the report said.

In Syria, where nearly 4 million displaced people have recently returned, people face worsening water scarcity and erratic rainfall, while flooding along the Euphrates River in May damaged homes and displaced thousands of people, the report said.

Across sub-Saharan Africa, one in three refugee settlements could experience at least 100 days of dangerous heat each year by 2050, threatening health and livelihoods, the report said. In some settlements in Ethiopia, including Helaweyn, dangerous heat could persist for more than 200 days a year, increasing the risks of heatstroke and premature death.

"Refugees often have limited access to cooling, water and reliable energy, making it harder to escape dangerous temperatures," the report said.

UNHCR also warned that a forecast supersized El Niño could worsen climate-related risks in many refugee-hosting countries and trigger further displacement.

In East Africa, severe flooding could displace up to 3 million people in Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan and Uganda by the end of this year, UNHCR said. In the Sahel, drought, flooding and conflict could intensify competition over scarce resources, while parts of Asia face heightened risks of droughts, floods and cyclones.

UNHCR called on governments and climate-finance institutions meeting at COP31 to increase funding for climate adaptation, highlighting that only about 10 per cent of climate finance reaches fragile or conflict-affected countries.

On Wednesday, a separate UN report found rich ​countries were falling well short of the $305 billion needed each year ‌to help developing nations adapt to climate change, even as extreme weather events become more frequent and severe.

item.description:
Another consignment of uranium imported from Russia for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant (RNPP) has reached the project site via an alternative route.
The nuclear fuel was transported to Rooppur in three specially designed trucks via Dhaka-Mawa Expressway, Padma Bridge, Faridpur, Rajbari and Kushtia.
At around 7:30 am on Friday, the convoy carrying uranium entered the project site under the supervision of the Bangladesh Army amid tight security provided by other law enforcement agencies.
Confirming the arrival of the uranium, Rooppur project Site In-charge KBM Ruhul Quddus said that the nuclear fuel was transported through an alternative route for the first time with tight security, in order to avoid the ongoing garment workers' movement in Gazipur and possible clashes.
The alternative route was used instead of the usual Dhaka-Tangail Highway and Jamuna Bridge, he said.
The convoy travelled from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital via Dhaka-Mawa Expressway, Padma Bridge, Bhanga in Faridpur, Rajbari, Kushtia and Lalon Shah Bridge at Pakshi before reaching Rooppur.
With the arrival, a total of five uranium consignments have reached the project site: two additional consignments for the first unit of the RNPP and three for the second unit.
Earlier, Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom had announced plans to transport 163 uranium fuel assemblies for the second unit of Rooppur in seven cargo aircraft, along with another 48 assemblies in two cargo flights for refueling the first unit.
In total, nine consignments of nuclear fuel are scheduled to be brought into the country.
The RNPP is being built with Russian technology, has two VVER-1200 reactor units.
Of the two units, the first unit has already begun activities under the 'Power Startup Stage-C' program. On October 29, the Chairman of the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) granted approval to begin these activities.
During Stage-C, the reactor's capacity will be gradually increased to test the performance of various plant components. According to the plan, the authorities have set a target of connecting approximately 300 megawatts of electricity from the first unit to the national grid on a trial basis in December.
However, this process will be carried out subject to fulfilling the conditions set by the regulatory authority and obtaining the necessary approvals.

item.title: 45th BCS: Re-Verification begins for excluded candidates, decision this month
item.description:
Out of the 1,807 candidates finally recommended by the Public Service Commission (PSC) for the 45th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS), 1,702 candidates were included in the official gazette notification. As a result, a total of 105 candidates were excluded from the final appointment gazette despite successfully clearing all examination stages.

The exclusion of such a significant number of candidates following the PSC's recommendation has sparked widespread discussion.

Recently, the Ministry of Public Administration clarified the specific reasons behind the exclusion of the 105 candidates. Among them, 49 failed to submit the required paperwork and legal documents on time. Meanwhile, the remaining 56 candidates were excluded due to police verification reports and other administrative reasons, despite possessing all valid documentation.

The government is now reviewing the cases of those candidates who were left out.

Hunger strike at Raju Sculpture and unwanted incident

Despite having no criminal records, the candidates excluded from the gazette took to the streets to protest. They staged a hunger strike and sit-in in front of the Raju Sculpture on the Dhaka University campus.

During the hunger strike, police picked up four candidates for questioning on suspicion of being affiliated with banned organizations. However, gazfollowing a preliminary inquiry that found no evidence of criminal involvement, police released them the following day.

The protesters said their movement was entirely non-political and a fight to claim their rights based on merit. Although the release of the candidates taken from the Raju Sculpture brought relief, they continue to demand the publication of a supplementary gazette.

Re-verification underway, government promises no injustice

The government has offered some relief amid uncertainty over the candidates left out of the gazette. A re-verification process has begun based on the candidates' permanent addresses to ensure that none of them faces injustice or discrimination.

Regarding the overall situation, State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari told Prothom Alo, "Of the 105 candidates left out, 49 could not submit the required documents. The government is taking the cases of those whose names were not included very seriously. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has given clear instructions that not a single candidate should be deprived of appointment unjustly."

The state minister confirmed, "The re-verification process based on the permanent addresses of those excluded from the gazette is now fully underway. We hope to complete the verification by the second week of this month. Those who were taken away from the Raju Sculpture have also been released. No candidate will be unjustly deprived of an opportunity within the legal framework."

45th BCS at a glance

The circular for the 45th BCS was published on 30 November 2022, drawing 346,000 applicants. The preliminary examination was held on 19 May 2023, with the results published on 6 June 2023, in which 12,789 candidates qualified.

The written examination took place in January 2024, followed by viva voce starting in July 2025.

After completing all stages, the PSC recommended 1,807 candidates for cadre posts on 27 November 2025. Nearly 11 months after the final recommendation, the Ministry of Public Administration published the appointment gazette for 1,702 candidates on 14 October 2026.

The entire recruitment process for the 45th BCS was completed after nearly four years, spanning the political tenures of three different governments.

item.title: Italian fashion brands Patrizia Pepe, Dixie under court supervision over labour exploitation in Bangladesh
item.description:
Italian fashion labels Patrizia Pepe and Dixie have been placed under court administration over the alleged exploitation of foreign workers in their supply chain in Tuscany, prosecutors and judicial sources said on Friday.

The measure targeted two companies that relied on unscrupulous subcontractors to lower production costs, Luca Tescaroli, chief prosecutor in the city of Prato, said in a statement, without naming them.

Judicial sources later confirmed the companies' identities.

A spokesperson for Patrizia Pepe had no immediate comment, while a spokesperson for Dixie did not immediately respond to a request from Reuters.

New wage structure for garment workers to take effect in December

Milan courts have taken similar moves in recent years against other well-known labels, including LVMH-owned LVMH.PA cashmere firm Loro Piana and units of fashion houses Valentino and Giorgio Armani, putting pressure on the entire Italian fashion industry to improve labour standards.

'Culpable inaction and no proper oversight'

Being placed under administration means that court-appointed external administrators will verify steps due to be taken by Patrizia Pepe and Dixie to meet judges' demands on the cleanup of their supply chains.

The two companies, however, are not under any criminal investigation.

The Florence court that placed them under supervision reprimanded them for "culpable inaction and failure to exercise proper oversight" on subcontractors who exploited Bangladeshi and Albanian workers, Tescaroli said.

The workers were poorly paid, forced to work long hours, denied holidays and constantly harassed and abused, Tescaroli said, adding that 18 of them who cooperated with investigators would be offered legal residence permits.

The prosecutor also said it was the first labour abuse case in the textile city of Prato involving Albanian subcontractors, saying they had adopted criminal practices traditionally associated with Chinese-owned sweatshops.

item.title: US offers $20m reward for info on Iran's nuclear program
item.description:
Washington is offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.

A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X.

The program was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of "continuity of knowledge" regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.

It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward.

Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran's nuclear program.

"If we didn't hit Iran, you wouldn't have Israel today," Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. "If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East."

But the president also said Iran -- which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war -- is eager to end the conflict.

"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.

Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.

And on Tuesday Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Earlier this week Trump said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

item.title: Why has growth of transactions through Bangla QR stalled?
item.description:
The ''Bangla QR'' initiative, launched to popularise digital transactions by reducing the use of cash, has stalled. Initially, the transaction pace was encouraging, but recently there has been a decline. Although Bangladesh Bank has set targets for banks and financial institutions to increase transactions.

Meanwhile, from this month, Bangla QR code service has been introduced for peer-to-peer transactions.

An analysis of Bangladesh Bank's data from May to October shows that in the last two weeks of May, daily transactions through Bangla QR amounted to Tk 2-3 billion. In the first week of October, daily transactions rose to Tk 13. 5 billion. After that, transactions began to decline. By the last week of October, transactions fell to Tk 11. 9 billion. Without new initiatives, there seems to be no immediate potential for growth in transactions, according to industry insiders.

An analysis of Bangladesh Bank's data from May to October shows that in the last two weeks of May, daily transactions through Bangla QR amounted to Tk 2-3 billion.

Regarding this, Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan said, "We don't understand why the pace of transactions through Bangla QR has decreased. Bangladesh Bank is trying to increase transactions by removing obstacles. If necessary, more initiatives will be taken to make Bangla QR universal."

Reasons for low response in transactions

In July, the use of Bangla QR code was made mandatory for transactions. Therefore, all banks and MFS had to install Bangla QR codes at the merchant level instead of their unique codes. Various banks and MFS institutions have given four to five Bangla QR codes against a single bank or MFS account of these merchants. This has become an alternative system for merchants scattered across the country to withdraw cash. This list of merchants includes everyone from rural shopkeepers to large service and product sellers. As a result, the MFS agent ecosystem has collapsed due to the influence of a large number of merchants.

Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain KhanWe don't understand why the pace of transactions through Bangla QR has decreased. Bangladesh Bank is trying to increase transactions by removing obstacles. If necessary, more initiatives will be taken to make Bangla QR universal.

From October, Bangladesh Bank made it free for sellers to receive money through Bangla QR. Therefore, merchants don't need to pay any fees to receive money from customers and return it in cash. In contrast, a specific fee is required to cash out from MFS agents like bKash, Nagad, and Rocket.

For this fee, MFS companies pay the government more than Tk 3 as revenue for every thousand. But there is no cost if the money is withdrawn through merchants. Additionally, merchants do not have to pay any revenue to the government. Therefore, withdrawing cash using this QR code is beneficial for both customers and merchants.

For the government and MFS companies, this poses a significant business obstacle. On 30 September, Bangladesh Bank announced that if money is withdrawn through Bangla QR to increase digital transactions, those accounts will be closed. Since then, MFS and banks have been closing accounts when money is withdrawn instead of purchasing. From then on, the pace of QR transactions has declined.

Initiatives to increase transactions

To boost transactions through Bangla QR code, Bangladesh Bank has allocated Tk 1 billion in the 2026-27 fiscal year to provide incentives to banks and MFS companies. Incentives are being provided for transactions up to Tk 2,000 at the stores of registered small and marginal vendors or service providers. Under this facility, the bank or MFS company that sets up the QR code at the merchant point gets an incentive of 0.10 per cent of the transaction. On the other hand, the issuing company through which the customer is paying receives an incentive of 0.20 per cent of the transaction. Yet, transactions are not increasing as expected.

Sonali Bank's Managing Director (MD) Shawkat Ali KhanWe have set targets for our employees to increase the use of Bangla QR. This is gradually increasing account openings and transactions. If everyone progresses this way, the service will grow.

Transaction scenario

The analysis of data shows that in 7 out of the last 24 weeks, QR transactions were negative. Industry insiders blame several technological and structural weaknesses for this stagnation in transactions. They believe that a large portion of the country's citizens are now customers of mobile banking services like bKash and Nagad. The service cannot be popularised without the active participation of these two companies. Additionally, customers need to be made aware, and infrastructure needs to be developed. It's also essential to make banking apps more user-friendly. The announced initiative to enable the use of the Bangla QR app without the internet also needs to be implemented.

Who is leading in Bangla QR?

In opening new merchant accounts with Bangla QR, Islami, Pubali, Janata, Sonali, and Rupali Bank are currently leading.

When asked, Sonali Bank's Managing Director (MD) Shawkat Ali Khan told Prothom Alo, "We have set targets for our employees to increase the use of Bangla QR. This is gradually increasing account openings and transactions. If everyone progresses this way, the service will grow."

item.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader sentenced to 200 years for child murders
item.description:
KENYA-CULT-CRIME-COURT-SHAKAHOLA

A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for the murder of 190 children and one adult in an infamous starvation cult.

Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the sect's base near the coastal resort of Malindi, in what became known as the "Shakahola Forest Massacre".

Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, was accused of inciting his followers to starve themselves to death to "meet Jesus".

He was convicted last month of murdering 191 people between January 2021 and September 2023, alongside 28 co-accused.

On Friday, the court sentenced him to 100 years for the homicide charges and 100 years for the starvation charges, while his accomplices -- many of whom starved their own children to death -- received a variety of lengthy prison terms.

"Children observed siblings drop dead... as their parents ate and drank," the judge said.

"Some died as a result of strangulation, severely beaten... Children were subjected to extreme suffering... terrifying living conditions, psychological trauma."

Mackenzie was impassive as the sentence was read out, as he had been throughout the trial.

Prosecutors had called for the death penalty, but the judge said it would "fail to achieve deterrence, particularly where the convicts regard death as a pathway to heaven and a union with Jesus and their deceased children."

Kenya has the death penalty but has not carried out an execution since 1987.

Francis Wanje, a 62-year-old teacher who lost two grandchildren to the cult, told AFP he had hoped Mackenzie would be sentenced to death to prevent further tragedies.

Another of his grandchildren, now 11, went without food for eight days before being rescued in March 2023.

He testified that his brothers, aged two and five, had died after their parents, acting on the guru's orders, forbade them from eating or drinking.

"Nothing can ease the pain," said Wanje, who blamed authorities for failing to act swiftly.

"I really have great (anger) towards the authorities. If they had taken action, we would not be here today," he added.

Death penalty

Mackenzie's lawyer said he would appeal the verdict. He also faces manslaughter and terrorism charges in other trials, which he denies.
Around 120 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial.

According to witnesses, the movement denounced formal education as "satanic", viewed modern medicine and hospitals as instruments of the devil and required followers to cut themselves off from the outside world.

Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 after a rights group alerted authorities and some followers were rescued from the 325-hectare (800-acre) ranch in the Shakahola forest on Kenya's coast.

The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights put the death toll at 429 in 2024. Some victims remain unidentified.

The case has fuelled calls for tighter regulation of religious organisations, after it emerged that Mackenzie had previously been arrested twice but released.

He established the Good News International Church in 2003 and set up branches in Nairobi and along Kenya's coast that attracted thousands of devotees, though he claimed it closed in 2019.

He was arrested in 2017 over charges of "radicalisation" but was acquitted. He was arrested again in 2019 in relation to two child deaths at Shakahola but released on bail.

item.title: PM announces pay rise for Gram Police, govt to pay mobile bills
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today, Saturday announced a pay rise for Gram Police, lifting their monthly salary from Tk 7,500 to Tk 10,500 and their chiefs’ from Tk 8,000 to Tk 11,000.

The government will also pay monthly mobile phone allowance up to Tk 150 for each member.

The Prime Minister said the new arrangements will take effect from today. He said two additional women Gram Police members would be recruited in every union and their maternity leave would be extended to six months.

The Prime Minister made the announcements at a rally of Gram Police at the National Parade Ground in the capital, marking the historic National Revolution and Solidarity Day.

“At present, a Gram Police member’s monthly salary is Tk 7,500. We have raised it to Tk 10,500. The monthly salary of the Gram Police chief has been raised from Tk 8,000 to Tk 11,000,” the Prime Minister declared.

“The retirement gratuity has been raised from Tk 50,000 to Tk 80,000 for members and from Tk 80,000 to Tk 1 lakh for chiefs,” he announced.

The Prime Minister said a member of Gram Police will get Tk 150 monthly mobile phone allowance to facilitate them communication easier.

item.description:
Gas supply to the national grid has returned to normal levels after Summit LNG’s floating terminal in Moheshkhali, Cox’s Bazar, resumed operations following maintenance.
The terminal restarted regasification at 1pm on Saturday, with Petrobangla confirming that both LNG terminals were once again supplying gas to the national grid at their usual levels.
According to Petrobangla’s data at 2pm on Saturday, the country’s total gas supply stood at 2,408 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd). Of this, 1,584mmcfd came from domestic gas fields, while LNG accounted for 824mmcfd.
The Summit terminal was shut down last Wednesday for maintenance, resulting in a significant drop in gas supply to the national grid.
At 8am that day, total gas supply stood at 2,540mmcfd, including 1,566mmcfd from domestic fields and 974mmcfd from LNG.
After the terminal was shut down, the total supply fell to 2,079mmcfd by 10am. Domestic gas supply remained almost unchanged at 1,565mmcfd, while LNG supply dropped to 514mmcfd.
This represented a decline of 461mmcfd in total supply within two hours.
Petrobangla had earlier said maintenance at the Summit terminal would continue from 8am on November 4 until 4pm on November 7, during which regasification would remain suspended. It had warned that the disruption could cause low gas pressure across the country.

item.description:
At least seven Bangladeshis, including women and children, were killed in a road accident in Saudi Arabia on Saturday.
The accident occurred on a highway while they were travelling from Medina to Jeddah, according to officials at the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah.
Consulate officials said the victims were travelling in a vehicle from Medina when the driver lost control, causing the crash. All seven died at the scene.
The deceased were associated with Al Abeir Cold Store Trading Company and hailed from Chakaria Upazila of Cox’s Bazar.
Nuruzzaman, the company’s marketing manager, said the victims included the company’s storekeeper Ziaur Rahman, his two sons and daughter, the wife of company forklift driver Ilias, and Alamshah, a storekeeper working in Mecca, along with his one-month-old daughter.

item.title: Dhaka plans two monorail routes by 2030
item.description:
The government is moving ahead with plans to build two monorail routes in Dhaka by 2030, with detailed design work underway following the completion of a pre-feasibility study.
Dhaka Transport Co-ordination Authority (DTCA) Additional Executive Director Dr Md Moshiur Rahman said the proposed monorail system would expand the capital’s public transport network by providing an environmentally friendly, sustainable and efficient transport option, particularly in areas with high passenger demand, reports BSS.
He said the proposed routes could be connected to existing and planned metro rail lines and other public transport services, making it easier for commuters to reach their final destinations from metro stations.
Consultants from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) have already completed the pre-feasibility study. The detailed designs are now being prepared and are expected to be submitted within six months, according to the project timeline.
The final two routes will be selected based on technical, economic and environmental assessments, taking into account passenger demand, potential benefits and financial viability.
Moshiur said the DTCA conducted transport modelling surveys in different parts of the capital to assess passenger demand and shared the findings with BUET consultants for analysis.
BUET's Bureau of Research, Testing and Consultation (BRTC) completed the pre-feasibility study. Under the agreement, the detailed designs are scheduled to be submitted within the next six months.
The government has allocated Tk7.57 crore from the revenue budget for the pre-feasibility study and detailed designs of the proposed two routes.
The revised Strategic Transport Plan proposes five monorail routes spanning around 79.4km. Authorities plan to select a priority route within three months and complete the overall study within six months.
The five preliminary routes were identified by considering areas where access to feeder bus services for mass rapid transit (MRT) lines is limited.
They are: Airport-Bashundhara via Purbachal and Jolshiri (25.2km); Moddho Badda-Bhulta (14.6km); Rampura-Demra (10.3km); Mohammadpur-Postogola (11.7km); and Airport-Savar via Uttara Centre (17.6km).
The proposal also mentions Monorail-8, from TSC at Dhaka University to Kamrangirchar, with nine stations; Monorail-10, from Alubdi to either West Agargaon or Shyamoli, with 10 stations; and Monorail-13, from Paltan to either Sadarghat or Jhilmil, with six or 11 stations.
A BUET consultant told BSS that the pre-feasibility study examined population patterns, potential passenger catchment areas around stations, gaps in public transport services, traffic congestion, land availability for depots and opportunities for future expansion.
The government-funded assessment will also examine proposed route alignments, potential station and depot locations, passenger demand, technical and structural suitability, economic feasibility, and environmental and social impacts.
A monorail runs on an elevated structure, making it a potential option for densely populated areas where road space is limited and conventional transport infrastructure may be difficult to build.
The study will assess construction and operating costs, passenger capacity and the overall economic and social justification for the proposed system. Local and expatriate Bangladeshi experts have been engaged as consultants.
The initiative is part of the government's broader efforts to ease traffic congestion and improve urban transport in the capital, in line with its election pledges.

item.title: Import exceeds export as current account deficit widens
item.description:
Bangladesh saw its current account deficit widen sharply in the first quarter of the current fiscal year as growing import far outstrips export with cascading fresh pressure on the external balance.
Current account, a key component of the balance of payments (BoP), recorded a deficit of $1.33 billion during the July-September period of FY27 in a swing from $821 million in the corresponding quarter a year earlier.
The tipping of balance between incomings and outgoings in terms of foreign trade in goods and services is reflected in the latest BoP data prepared by the central bank.
The data show the widening deficit also dragged down the overall balance-of-payments pendulum.
It swung to a deficit of $1.16 billion during the quarter, signifying a growing pressure on the country's external transactions-and hence on its foreign-exchange buffers.
The deterioration came as export earnings grew by only around 7% year on year while import payments expanded over 15% during the period, the data show.
The faster growth in imports, due mainly to price hike of petroleum products amid the Middle East crisis, than exports widened the trade gap.
However, stronger remittance inflows had supported significantly to bridge the gaps.
Remittances inflows from expatriate Bangladeshis grew by 13.3% during the period, helping lower the pressures on the external sector.
Economists warn Bangladesh's widening current account deficit (CAD), driven largely by rising import payments, could build up pressure on the foreign-exchange market and complicate efforts to maintain-exchange rate stability.
They have urged the central bank and policymakers to adopt prudent, market-oriented measures to absorb the external shock, while cautioning against excessive intervention in the currency market or a return to multiple exchange rates.
The widening deficit signals that the country's foreign-currency outflows are increasingly exceeding inflows, raising concerns over the sustainability of the external balance if the trend persists.
Economists say prolonged pressure could lead to further depletion of foreign-exchange reserves, exchange rate volatility and higher import costs, which might heat up domestic inflation.
Dr Zahid Hussain, former lead economist at the World Bank Dhaka office, said that the government should avoid repeating the exchange rate management policies adopted in 2022, when it maintained multiple exchange rates in an attempt to contain pressure on the taka.
Instead, the authorities should allow market-based decisions to guide the exchange rate, avoiding administrative controls and excessive intervention that could undermine market confidence.
The former World Bank economist notes that the current external shock is still manageable, as Bangladesh retained sufficient foreign-exchange reserves to meet its import-payment obligations.
Hussain pointed out that current-account payment increased by around 11% during the July-September quarter, while corresponding inflows grew by approximately 9%, indicating a widening mismatch between foreign-currency earning and spending.
He suggested policymakers should focus on maintaining orderly market conditions rather than attempting to suppress exchange-rate movements through restrictive measures.
